chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who forgets to say the Takbir during the Days of Tashriq. He said: 'If he forgets until he rises from his place, there is no penalty upon him.'
As for the voluntary prayer, there is no Takbir after it; that is indicated by what he narrated.

key_terms.أَيَّامِ التَّشْرِيقِ: Days of Tashriq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets to say Takbir during the Days of Tashriq?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on returning to Mina and stoning the Jamarat, this hadith establishes the principle of *al-asl fi al-ibadat al-suhul* (ease in worship) by absolving the worshipper of penalty if the time for the specific Takbir passes before they rise from their place. It further clarifies that the ritual Takbir is not a recurring requirement after every voluntary prayer, distinguishing between obligatory ritual markers and general devotional practices. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on removing undue hardship during the intense rituals of Hajj.
